summary.headline: AIA Q4 FY26 revenue INR1,251 crore and PAT INR393 crore, a record quarter helped by INR65 crore FX gain; management guides realisation INR165/kg as sustainable.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 sales were 70,000 tonnes against 68,000 tonnes a year earlier, with revenue of INR1,251 crore and EBITDA of INR502 crore; management called it the highest-ever quarterly EBITDA and PAT. Full-year FY26 volume was 258,000 tonnes (flat vs 255,000) with revenue INR4,355 crore, EBITDA INR1,744 crore and PAT INR1,270 crore. Management attributed part of the quarter to one-offs: INR65 crore FX gain, a product-mix tilt to castings, and a lower tax rate. The main narrative was a South American large-mine trial win for a lining plus new-generation discharge system solution, with a second mine conversion ordered, but no volume guidance was given.

Management called it the highest ever
Includes treasury income INR67 crore, FX gain INR65 crore, export benefits INR15 crore

segments.name: Mining
segments.commentary: Q4 volume about 45,000 tonnes and FY26 about 160,000 tonnes of the 258,000 total. Mining conversion win in South America was the key update.

segments.name: Non-mining
segments.commentary: Q4 volume about 25,000 tonnes and FY26 about 98,000 tonnes, the balance of total volume. No segment-level revenue or margin disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Realisation of INR165/kg is the sustainable planning figure for FY27; Q4's INR178 is partly one-off (FX and castings mix).
Management said a volume growth guidance is premature; no FY27 volume number given.
Operating margin excluding other income is about 28-29%; as grinding media mix rises, margin may trend to 24-26% in percentage terms while absolute profit grows.

Capex for India: total INR100-150 crore for maintenance and renewable balancing (INR60-100 crore maintenance plus about INR30 crore renewable balance). Ghana and China plants are under approval paperwork and slowed.
Renewable power to reach about 60-65% of consumption by June-July 2026, with about 100 MW rated capacity; expected cost INR5-5.5/unit vs grid cost, saving about INR1.5/unit.
Tax rate for FY26 about 2 percentage points lower than normal; effective Q4 tax rate near 16% due to one-offs (INR25-30 crore lower tax).
risks_watch: FX tailwind: INR65 crore FX gain in Q4 (about 4-5% of EBITDA); management says rupee weakness will be partly passed through to customers over a quarter or two.
Mine conversion is early: no volume guidance; second mine outcome expected in the next couple of months; time to market for new solutions uncertain.
Global shipping and geopolitical risk (Iran war, freight volatility, transit up 10-15 days) and rising raw material costs.
Ghana and China plants are on hold; the company says they are not shelved.
Low utilisation at about 55%; cash of about INR4,300 crore reduces ROCE (management says ROCE is about 22%, could be 35-37% without cash).

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable annual volume will the South American mine conversion add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to give volume numbers; the strategy is a shift to lining plus discharge-system solutions, with grinding media to follow, and volume guidance is premature.

qa_highlights.question: Did the new client give initial orders, and what is the utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The client gave an order for a second mine conversion after the successful trial; overall capacity utilisation is about 55%, with capacity for up to 70-75%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 23% quarterly operating margin sustainable given China and Ghana slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating margin excluding other income is 28-29% today; as grinding media mix rises, margin in percentage terms may fall to 24-26% while absolute profit grows. Ghana and China are not shelved.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need more capacity, and what expansion options exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Current 436,000 tonnes capacity can take utilisation to 70-75%; the paused GIDC Kerala brownfield can add 50,000-75,000 tonnes in 6-12 months, and Ghana land is finalised for 50,000 tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise about 25% year on year with flat volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock is built against orders: a South American order from Oct-Nov 2025 and a billing-cycle change for another customer (billing moved to consumption) converted revenue into stock; not housekeeping.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 tax rate near 16%, and why did short-term borrowings fall to zero?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 included final tax true-up, a refund of about INR15 crore in a subsidiary and a deferred tax asset in another; Q4 one-offs were about INR25-30 crore lower tax. Borrowing reduction was treasury arbitrage, cyclical, with no specific reason.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for the INR4,300 crore cash pile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is held deliberately until solution efficacy is proven; ROCE is about 22% and could be 35-37% without the cash; it asked for 6-12 more months and denied any takeover or buyout.

qa_highlights.question: How do realisations behave given the sharp rupee depreciation and the casting mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the realisation rise reflects raw material cost, shipping pass-through, currency (INR75-80 to about INR95) and mix; it guided INR165/kg and said well above that may not be fair as the package includes castings and grinding media.

capex_capacity: Current capacity 436,000 tonnes against FY26 production of 258,000 tonnes; management says utilisation can rise to 70-75%, which would allow about 350,000 tonnes, with overall utilisation about 55% currently.
Brownfield expansion at GIDC, Kerala (near Ahmedabad) paused; can add 50,000-75,000 tonnes in 6-12 months once traction shows, with land and infrastructure available.

Ghana (land and location finalised) and China (about 100,000 tonnes combined planned capacity) are in a slowdown mode pending approval paperwork; management says they are not shelved and can be accelerated.
FY26 capex about INR130 crore; no spend other than Ghana and China planned this year, with those projects still at paperwork stage and no cost estimate given.
India capex outflow guided at INR100-150 crore in total: INR60-100 crore maintenance, balancing and cost-saving capex, plus about INR30 crore to complete the renewable portfolio.

Captive renewable power to reach about 100 MW rated capacity by June-July 2026, meeting about 60-65% of about 30 crore units annual consumption (about 20 crore units), at an expected INR5-5.5/unit versus grid, saving about INR1.5/unit.
demand_pricing: South American large-mine trial succeeded with a lining system plus new-generation discharge system; the customer has placed an order for a second mine conversion, with outcome on the second mine expected in the next couple of months.

Management declined to give volume guidance, calling it premature; no sustainable volume figure for the new conversion, and the addressable market is cited as 800,000-1 million tonnes of ore processing across gold and copper mines.
Earlier 15,000-tonne order from a South American mine: dispatches began in October 2025 from India, with invoicing to step up from roughly Jan-Feb 2026 and regular flow from Q1 FY27.

Realisation: Q4 FY26 about INR178/kg, FY26 INR165/kg; management says INR165/kg is the sustainable planning figure, with about 4-5% of EBITDA coming from the INR65 crore FX gain and a higher casting mix in Q4.
Operating margin excluding other income about 28-29% today; as grinding media mix rises, percentage margin may fall to 24-26% while absolute profit grows.
Capacity utilisation about 55% overall; castings production has risen but capacity is adequate for the next couple of years.
Brazil volumes about 6,000-8,000 tonnes, not yet scaled up after the sunset review.
Raw material costs at high levels with the Iran war, shipping transit extended by 10-15 days; shipping costs have eased from post-war peak; management says it works on 100% pass-through.
Currency moved from about INR75-80 to about INR95/USD; customers outside the US import in local currency, so benefit is retained for a quarter or two until dollar prices are reset.
Anti-dumping and duty measures in multiple countries: status quo continues, per management.
key_quotes: So, when we say that China and Ghana are slowing down, we don't mean to say that we have shelved them.
It is too early for us to give you any clear-cut idea about X volume, Y volume.
At least 15% of throughput improvement, at least. Otherwise, it's not material.
So, it's not just something that anybody can walk in.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the South American trial and long-term solution strategy, but cautious and evasive on volume, timelines and the second mine, repeatedly declining to quantify. Management was defensive on cash deployment and on the Q4 one-offs, which it framed as temporary.

Ghana plant (land and location finalised), slowed pending approval paperwork, no cost estimate

growth.why: No FY27 volume or revenue guidance; management called volume guidance premature, with realisation of INR165/kg as the planning figure and a second South American mine conversion order as the main demand signal, while utilisation sits at about 55% of 436,000 t and the Kerala brownfield and Ghana/China projects are paused or slowed.
